rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hereafter and this world belong to God as creator and owner; He alone has complete sovereignty, while every creature is inherently deficient.
rows.anchor: له الآخرة والأولى خلقا وملكا ، فهو الملك المالك صاحب الملك التام . فأما المخلوق فالنقص لازم للكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels' intercession benefits nothing unless God permits and approves it; this rebuts the claim that angels are their intercessors with God.
rows.anchor: وهذا رد عليهم حيث قالوا : إن الملائكة شفعاؤنا عند الله

words: إن الذين لا يؤمنون بالأخرة ليسمون الملائكة تسمية الأنثى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny the afterlife call angels female without knowledge or verification, following conjecture, which yields no truth.
rows.anchor: هذه التسمية من عندهم ، وهم لا يتبعون فيها علما أو تحقيقا . . . بل ظنا - والظن لا يفيد شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to turn from those who reject the Qur’an, faith, and reflection on its meanings and want only worldly life; their knowledge stops there because they do not know the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أعرض عمن أعرض عن القرآن والإيمان به وتدبر معانيه ، ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا

words: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who is astray and who is guided, and recompenses each according to what that person deserves.
rows.anchor: وإن ربك عليم بالضال ، عليم بالمهتدي . . . وهو يجازي كلا بما يستحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns everything in heaven and earth in order to punish those who do wrong and reward those who do good with the best reward.
rows.anchor: يجزي الذين أساؤوا بالعقوبات ، ويجزي الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All sins are grave because they oppose God's command, though some are greater than others; nothing is greater than associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: الذنوب كلها كبائر لأنها مخالفة لأمر الله ، ولكن بعضها أكبر من بعض . ولا شيء أعظم من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses al-fawāḥish as sins or acts of disobedience.
rows.anchor: الفواحش } المعاصي . { إلا اللمم

rows.speaker: تكلموا فيه وقالوا
rows.claim: One reported view makes the exception disconnected: lammam is neither sin nor part of the indecencies.
rows.anchor: تكلموا فيه ، وقالوا : إنه استثناء منقطع ، واللمم ليس بإثم ولا من جملة الفواحش

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another view includes lammam among the indecencies but treats it as ambiguous, with God promising to forgive it.
rows.anchor: ويقال : اللمم من جملة الفواحش ولكن فيها اشتباها - فأخبر أنه يغفرها

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: A reported definition of lammam is committing the lapse and then abandoning it through repentance.
rows.anchor: ويقال : اللمم هو أن يأتي المرء ذلك ثم يقلع عنه بالتوبة

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities define lammam as a single occurrence of adultery, wine drinking, theft, or similar sin that the person does not repeat.
rows.anchor: وقال لعض السلف : هو الوقعة من الزنا تحصل مرة ثم لا يعود إليها ، وكذلك شرب الخمر ، والسرقة

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another view calls lammam the intention to commit a lapse without actually doing it.
rows.anchor: ويقال : هو أن يهم بالزلة ثم لا يفعلها

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another reported explanation of lammam is looking.
rows.anchor: ويقال : هو النظر

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another view defines lammam as sins that carry no prescribed legal penalty and are expiated by the prayers.
rows.anchor: ويقال : ما لا حد عليه من المعاصي ، وتكفر عنه الصلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qushayrī prefers a disconnected exception: lammam is not among the sins.
rows.anchor: والأصح أنه استثناء منقطع وأن اللمم ليس من جملة المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being created from the earth refers to the creation of Adam.
rows.anchor: إذ أنشأكم من الأرض } : يغني خلق آدم

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Self-praise signals that a person is veiled from God; one absorbed in witnessing the Lord does not praise himself.
rows.anchor: ويقال : تزكية النفس من علامات كون المرء محجوبا عن الله ؛ لأن المجذوب إلى الغاية والمستغرق في شهود ربه لا يزكي نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who is Godfearing better than people know themselves.
rows.anchor: { هو أعلم بمن اتقى } : لأنه أعلم بكم منكم

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: A person who believes anyone on earth is worse than himself is arrogant; a Muslim should view every other Muslim as better, imagining elders more obedient and youth less sinful.
rows.anchor: ويقال : من اعتقد أن على البسيطة أحدا شر منه فهو متكبر . ويقال : المسلم يجب أن يكون بحيث يرى كل مسلم خيرا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person described as turning away has turned away from the truth.
rows.anchor: أعرض عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small amount given is charity, and akdā means he cut off or stopped his giving.
rows.anchor: وتصدق بالقليل . { وكدى } أي قطع عطاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asking whether he sees means asking whether he knows the truth of the matter.
rows.anchor: { فهو يرى } : فهو يعلم صحة ذلك

rows.speaker: يقال
rows.claim: One report identifies the person as a hypocrite who helps with jihad briefly and then stops, as if he knew his unseen afterlife state.
rows.anchor: يقال : هو المنافق الذي يعين على الجهاد قليلا ثم يقطع ذلك : { أعنده علم الغيب } : فهو يرى حاله في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever is asked whether he has heard what is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, who fulfilled what was required of him in himself, wealth, and child.
rows.anchor: أم لم ينبأ هذا الكافر بما في صحف موسى ، وصحف إبارهيم الذي وفى ؛ أي أتم ما طولب به في نفسه وماله وولده

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People's striving differs: worldly pursuit loses, pursuit of Paradise profits, disciplining the self reaches God's approval, and striving in spiritual aspiration is thanked by God and guided to Him.
rows.anchor: الناس في سعيهم مختلفون ؛ فمن كان سعيه في طلب الدنيا خسرت صفقته ، ومن كان سعيه في طلب الجنة ربحت صفقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinner who strives to seek forgiveness and regrets the darkening of his record will receive reward, nearness, honor, and intimacy from God.
rows.anchor: وأما المذنب - فإذا كان سعيه في طلب غفرانه ، وندم القلب على ما اسود من ديوانه ، فسوف يجد من الله الثواب والقربة والكرامة والزلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who counts his breaths with God, attends to every shortcoming, and neglects no command will see his effort thanked in this life and the next; God addresses him directly as forgiven and thanked.
rows.anchor: ومن كان سعيه في عد أنفاسه مع الله ؛ لا يعرج على تقصير ، ولا يفرط في مأمور فسيرى جزاء سعيه مشكورا في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fullest recompense is the greatest and most exalted reward, neither cut off nor withheld.
rows.anchor: هو الجزاء الأكبر والأجل ، جزاء غير مقطوع ولا ممنوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final destination is return to God: things begin with Him through creation and end with Him through return.
rows.anchor: إليه المرجع والمصير ، فابتداء الأشياء من الله خلقا . وانتهاء الأشياء إلى الله مصيرا

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: One saying advises silence when speech reaches God.
rows.anchor: ويقال : إذا انتهى الكلام إلى الله تعالى فاسكتوا

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: One saying holds that after a servant reaches knowledge of God, only further divine kindnesses remain, such as gifts, fulfilled hopes, and states.
rows.anchor: ويقال : إذا وصل العبد إلى معرفة الله فليس بعده شيء إلا ألطافا من مال أو منال أو تحقيق آمال أو أحول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes laughter and weeping according to His will; they are shares allotted to His servants.
rows.anchor: يجريها على مراده - وهي حظوظ للعباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse first means ordinary human laughter and crying, which God brings about and creates.
rows.anchor: أراد به الضحك والبكاء المتعارف عليهما بين الناس ؛ فهو الذي يجريه ويخلقه

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: A metaphorical reading says God makes the earth laugh with vegetation and the sky weep with rain.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أضحك الأرض بالنبات ، وأبكى السماء بالمطر

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another reading says He makes Paradise's people laugh with Paradise and Hell's people weep with Hell.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أضحك أهل الجنة بالجنة ، وأبكى أهل النار بالنار

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another reading says the believer laughs in the afterlife and weeps in this life, while the unbeliever laughs here and weeps in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أضحك المؤمن في الآخرة وأبكاه في الدنيا ، وأضحك الكافر في الدنيا وأبكاه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another reading distinguishes outward laughter from inward weeping of the heart.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أضحكهم في الظاهر ، وأبكاهم بقلوبهم

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another reading says God makes believers' hearts laugh through forgiveness and unbelievers weep through humiliation.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أضحك المؤمن في الآخرة بغفرانه ، وأبكى الكافر بهوانه

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: For the gnostics, contentment makes their hearts laugh, while fear of separation makes their eyes weep.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أضحك قلوب العارفين بالرضا ، وأبكى عيونهم بخوف الفراق

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another reading attributes their laughter to God's mercy and the enemies' weeping to His wrath.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أضحكهم برحمته ، وأبكى الأعداء بسخطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes death in this world and life in the grave, where a person either rests or experiences punishment.
rows.anchor: أماته في الدنيا ، وأحياه في القبر ؛ فالقبر إما للراحة وإما للإحساس بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another explanation is death in this life followed by life at the resurrection.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أماته في الدنيا ، وأحياه في الحشر

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: A Sufi reading says ascetics' selves die through spiritual struggle, while gnostics' hearts live through witnessing.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أمات نفوس الزاهدين بالمجاهدة ، وأحيا قلوب العارفين بالمشاهدة

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Other inward pairings are death through awe and life through intimacy, concealment and manifestation, turning away and turning toward, and obedience and sin.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أماتها بالهيبة ، وأحياها بالأنس . ويقال : بالاستتار ، والتجلي . ويقال : بالإعراض عنه ، والإقبال عليه . ويقال : بالطاعة ، والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called a pair because the two sexes are joined when they are created from the drop of fluid.
rows.anchor: سماهما زوجين لازدواجهما عند خلقهما من النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aghnā means that God gave wealth, while aqnā means that He increased a person's possessions.
rows.anchor: { أغنى } : أعطى الغنى ، { وأقنى } : أكثر القنية أي المال

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Another gloss makes aqnā mean making someone need wealth, so the verse means God created both riches and poverty.
rows.anchor: وقيل { وأقنى } : أي أحوجه إلى المال - فعلى هذا يكون المعنى : أنه خلق الغنى والفقر

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Other glosses relate the words to contentment: aqnā means satisfying a person with what He gave, while aghnā means making content and aqnā means satisfying.
rows.anchor: ويقال : { وأقنى } أي أرضاه بما أعطاه . ويقال : { أغنى } أي أقنع ، { وأقنى } : أي أرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-shiʿrā is a star that rises after the Pleiades in intense heat; the Khuzaʿa worshipped it, so God declares Himself its Lord.
rows.anchor: الشعرى : كوكب يطلع بعد الجوزاء في شدة الحر ، وكانت خزاعة تعبدها فأعلم الله أنه رب معبودهم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ʿĀd are the people of Hūd, while the later ʿĀd are Iram of the pillars; God left none of Thamūd alive.
rows.anchor: عاد الأولى هم قوم هود ، وعاد الأخرى هي إرم ذات العماد ، كما أهلك ثمودا فما أبقى منهم أحدا

words: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِّن قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed Noah's people earlier; they were more unjust and transgressive than others because of their long lives and strong bodies.
rows.anchor: وأهلك من قبلهم قوم نوح الذين كانوا أظلم من غيرهم وأغوى لطول أعمارهم ، وقوة أجسادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overturned place is the towns of Lot's people, overturned by Gabriel; God lifted them from their roots, reversed them, and cast them down under punishment.
rows.anchor: أي المخسوف بها ، وهي قرى قوم لوط ، قلبها جبريل عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awhā means God dropped the towns to earth after uprooting and overturning them, then covered them with punishment.
rows.anchor: { أهوى } أي : أسقطها الله إلى الأرض بعدما اقتلعها من اصلها ، ثم عكسها وألقاها في الأرض ، فغشاها ما غشاها من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting God's favors and kindnesses, the verse asks which of His blessings a person can doubt.
rows.anchor: فبأي آلاء ربك - أيها الإنسان - تتشكك ؟ وقد ذكر هذا بعد ما عد إنعامه عليهم وإحسانه إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning refers to Muhammad, sent as a warner just as earlier messengers were sent.
rows.anchor: هو محمد ، أرسلناه نذيرا كما أرسلنا الرسل الآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Resurrection has drawn near; only God can bring it about, and once He does, no one can avert or uncover it.
rows.anchor: أي قربت القيامة . ولا يقدر أحد على إقامتها إلا الله ، وإذا أقامها فلا يقدر أحد على ردها وكشفها إلا الله

words: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: A Sufi saying calls the knowers' spiritual Resurrection recurrent: it happens several times in a day through estrangement, separation, and parting, and no one but God removes it.
rows.anchor: ويقال : إذا قامت قيامة هذه الطائفة - اليوم - فليس لها كاشف غيره . وقيامتهم تقوم في اليوم غير مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address asks whether they marvel at the Qur'an, doubt it, and mock it.
rows.anchor: أفمن هذا القرآن تعجبون ، وتكونون في شك ، وتستهزئون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāmidūn means heedless or distracted.
rows.anchor: { وأنتم سامدون } : أي لاهون . . .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are commanded to prostrate to God and worship no one besides Him.
rows.anchor: فاسجدوا لله ولا تعبدوا سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about God's punishment and warnings is phrased to magnify their gravity.
rows.anchor: قالها على جهةالتعظيم لأمره . وقد ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Noah is given with the most eloquent expression, the fewest words, and the fullest meaning.
rows.anchor: أفصح بيان وأقصر كلام وأتم معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah lived longer than the other prophets and endured affliction more intensely than they did.
rows.anchor: وكان نوح - عليه السلام - أطول الأنبياء عمرا ، وأشدهم للبلاء مقاساة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Noah's people perished, God preserved Noah and his children; the people of the earth descend from Noah's children.
rows.anchor: لما نجى نوحا متعه بعد هلاك قومه ومتع أولاده ، فكل من على وجه الأرض من أولا د نوح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story gives religious people hope: God soon destroys their enemies, enables them to possess their lands, and grants victory to His allies, as with Moses and Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: فإن الله يهلك - عن قريب - عدوهم ، ويمكنهم من ديارهم وبلادهم ، ويورثهم ما كان إليهم . وكذلك كانت قصة موسى عليه السلام مع فرعون وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes Qur'an recitation easy on tongues and its knowledge, understanding, and memorization easy in the hearts of different groups; all are people of the Qur'an and God's elect.
rows.anchor: يسرنا قراءته على ألسنة الناس ، ويسرنا علمه على قلوب قوم ، ويسرنا فهمه على قلوب قوم ، ويسرنا حفظه على قلوب قوم

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: A Sufi saying describes God communicating through the Qur'an with some spirits before they entered bodies, and asks whether anyone will remember that covenant.
rows.anchor: ويقال : كاشف الأرواح من قوم - بالقرآن - قبل إدخالها في الأجساد . { فهل من مدكر } لهذا العهد الذي جرى لنا معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also means that recitation and memorization have been made easy; no other revealed book is memorized in its entirety like the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: هونا قراءته وحفظه ؛ فليس كتاب من كتب الله تعالى يقرأ ظهرا إلا القرآن

words: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًۭا صَرْصَرًۭا فِى يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣarṣar wind is intensely cold and forceful, making a sound; the ill-omened day carried continuous punishment for eight days and seven nights.
rows.anchor: أي : باردة شديدة الهبوب ، يسمع لها صوت

words: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds pulled people from their dug shelters until they resembled the detached lower trunks of palm trees.
rows.anchor: تنزع رياحه الناس عن حفرهم التي حفروها . حتى صاروا كأنهم أسافل نخل منقطع

words: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍۢ
rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Another report says the wind tore their heads from their shoulders and left them like palm trunks whose tops had been cut off.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانت الريح تقتلع رؤوسهم عن مناكبهم ثم تلقي بهم كأنهم أصول نخل قطت رؤوسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated refrain stresses that God made Qur'an recitation and memorization easy.
rows.anchor: هونا قراءته وحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd, the people of Ṣāliḥ, rejected the warnings and objected to following a single human from among them; their camel-slaying story was related earlier.
rows.anchor: هم قوم صالح . وقد مضى القول فيه ، وما كان من عقرهم للناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a single blast that caused their destruction, leaving them like dry, withered vegetation.
rows.anchor: إلى أن أرسل الله عليهم صيحة واحدة أوجبت هذا الهلاك ، فصيرهم كالهشيم ، وهو اليابس من النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muḥtaẓir is what has been placed in an enclosure or what is contained inside one.
rows.anchor: { المحتظر } : أي : المجعول في الحظيرة ، أو الحاصل في الحظيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ruling resolved the dispute brought before the Prophet, made the transgressor bear the burden of his deed, and restored the woman's right; every hardship eventually passes.
rows.anchor: فارتفاع الأمر حتى وصوله إلى مجلس النبي ، والتحاكم لديه حمل المتعدي عناء فعلته ، وأعاد للمرأة حقها

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآدُّونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ كُبِتُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who oppose God's command and disobey the Messenger are humiliated, as earlier unbelievers and sinners were.
rows.anchor: الذين يخالفون أمر الله ويتركون طاعة رسول الله أذلوا وخذلوا ، كما أذل الذين من قبلهم من الكفار والعصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established practice is to punish criminals; neglecting the Prophet's Sunna or introducing religious innovation brings a person into this company and humiliation.
rows.anchor: وقد أجرى الله سنته بالانتقام من أهل الإجرام ؛ فمن ضيع للرسول سنة ، وأحدث في دينه بدعة انخرط في هذا السلك

words: يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعًۭا فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection, a person's deeds are shown and recalled as though the person stood at the scene of the lapse, feeling shame and regret that eclipse every punishment.
rows.anchor: إذا حوسب أحد في القيامة على عمله تصور له ما فعله وتذكره ، حتى كأنه قائم في تلك الحاله عن بساط الزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Muslim should avoid disobeying the Master; if a lapse occurs, keep it in mind and turn to God with earnest supplication.
rows.anchor: فسبيل المسلم ألا يحوم حول مخالفة أمر مولاه ، فإن جرى المقدور ووقع في هجنة التقصير فلتكن زلته على بال

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's accompanying presence is universal through knowledge and, specifically, through grace and aid; its mention profoundly affects the hearts of knowers and leads them into ecstatic absorption.
rows.anchor: معية الحق - سبحانه - وإن كانت على العموم بالعلم والرواية ، وعلى الخصوص بالفضل والنصرة - فلهذا الخطاب في قلوب أهل المعرفة أثر عظيم

words: مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجْوَىٰ ثَلَٰثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave companions are described as three with their dog fourth, whereas in God's account of private counsel He is the fourth; the two kinds of companionship are worlds apart.
rows.anchor: فشتان بين من رابعه كلبه وبين من رابعه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of spiritual purity have no remnant of worldly attachments; those who retain any are superficial seekers, not realized Sufis.
rows.anchor: وأهل الصفاء لم تبق عليهم من هذه الأشياء بقية ، وأما من بقي عليه منها شيء فمترسم سوقي

words: وَمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ فَٱنتَهُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse establishes the duty to follow the Messenger and adhere to his path and conduct, a principle elaborated in legal learning.
rows.anchor: هذا أصل من أصول وجوب متابعته ، ولزوم طريقته وسيرته - وفي العلم تفصيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant must test inspirations and unveiled spiritual states against religious knowledge; anything rejected by Qur'an and Sunna is misguidance.
rows.anchor: عرض ما وقع له من الخواطر وما يكاشف به من الأحوال على العلم - فما لا يقبله الكتاب والسنة فهو في ضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The booty is for the poor emigrants, about one hundred men, expelled from their homes and property; God's bounty means provision and His pleasure means the reward of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: يريد أن هذا الفيء لهؤلاء الفقراء الذين كانوا مقدار مائة رجل

words: وَيَنصُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their support is support for God's religion; being truthful is spiritually realized by a poor person who abandons attachments, devotes time to worship, inclines only to God, and accepts His decree.
rows.anchor: والفقير الصادق هو الذي يترك كل سبب وعلاقة ، ويفرغ أوقاته لعبادة الله

words: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلْإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns the Anṣār, who settled in Medina before the emigrants came from Mecca.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في الأنصار . { تبوءو الدار } أي سكنوا المدينة قبل المهاجرين

words: وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣār neither resented the emigrants' share of the booty nor inwardly objected to God's choice of them, even when they themselves were in need.
rows.anchor: ولا يحسدونهم على ذلك ، ولا يعترضون بقلوبهم على حكم الله بتخصيص المهاجرين ، حتى لو كانت بهم حاجة أو اختلال أحوال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about an Anṣārī who received a sheep's head and passed it among seven households until it returned to the first.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت الآية في رجل منهم أهديت له رأس شاة فطاف على سبعة أبيات حتى انتهى إلى الأول

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed about a man who served food to his guest and extinguished the lamp to make the guest think he was eating, preferring him and his family over himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل نزلت في رجل منهم نزل به ضيف فقرب منه الطعام وأطفأ السراج ليوهم ضيفه أنه يأكل

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: A saying calls the generous person one who builds a house for guests and brethren, and the miser one who builds for himself.
rows.anchor: ويقال : الكريم من بنى الدار لضيفانه وإخوانه ( واللئيم من بناها لنفسه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says whoever is protected from the self's stinginess, not merely whoever avoids stinginess.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لم يقل الله : ومن يتق شح نفسه بل قال : { ومن يوق شح نفسه }

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: One saying describes altruism as giving preference to a person who is already full while oneself remains hungry.
rows.anchor: ويقال : صاحب الإيثار يؤثر الشبعان على نفسه - وهو جائع

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another saying denies true altruism to anyone who distinguishes between people; the altruist prefers everyone without distinction.
rows.anchor: ويقال : من ميز بين شخص وشخص فليس بصاحب إيثار حتى يؤثر الجميع دون تمييز

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Altruism sees what others hold as theirs and what comes into one's own hand as a trust awaiting permission to use.
rows.anchor: ويقال : الإيثار أن ترى أن ما بأيدي الناس لهم ، وأن ما يحصل في يدك ليس إلا كالوديعة والأمانة عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God's beauty appears to a servant's heart, its thoughts gather around divine generosity; when His majesty appears to the secret heart, the self is consumed in Him and forgets this world and the hereafter.
rows.anchor: إذا تجلى لقلب عبد بوصف جماله تجمعت أفكاره على بساط جوده فلم يتفرق بسواه . ومن تجلى لسره بنعت جلاله اندرجت جملته ، واستهلك في وجوده

words: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The realized Sufis' secrets swim in the shoreless seas of God's unity and cannot depart; they set the jewels of individuation in a crown of gnosis to wear at meeting God.
rows.anchor: تسبح في بحار توحيد الحق أسرار أهل التحقيق ، وبحرهم بلا شاطىء ؛ فبعد ما حصلوا فيها فلا خروج ولا براح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Malik is the sovereign alone entitled to majesty; al-Quddūs is the one exalted beyond perception and attainment.
rows.anchor: { الملك } : الملك المتفرد باستحقاق الجبروت . { القدوس } : المنزه عن الدرك والوصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creatures can know realities only while affirming God's transcendence and reflecting on His acts; His essence cannot be observed, apprehended, or encompassed in knowledge.
rows.anchor: فليس بيد الخلق إلا عرفان الحقائق بنعت التعالي ، والتأمل في شهود أفعاله ، فأما الوقوف على حقيقة أنيته - فقد جلت الصمدية عن إشراف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about transcendence is accompanied by an unidentified poem: the crescent lights the night traveler but does not host him.
rows.anchor: وقلن بنا : نحن الأهلة إنما . . . نضيء لمن يسري بليل ولا نقري

words: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّۦنَ رَسُولًۭا مِّنْهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Muhammad unlettered and free from acquired learning, then raised him above all with noble qualities; as an orphan He sheltered him, and likewise gave him knowledge without study, clothing him in honor and manifesting realities through him.
rows.anchor: جرده كل تكلف لتعلم ، وعن الاتصاف بتطلب . ثم بعثه فيهم وأظهر عليه من الأوصاف ما فاق الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The others include non-Arabs and later generations through the Resurrection, since Muhammad was sent to all people.
rows.anchor: أي بعثه في الأميين ، وفي آخرين منهم وهم العجم ، ومن يأتي . . إلى يوم القيامة ؛ فهو مبعوث إلى لناس كافة

words: ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grace here means prophethood, which God grants as He wills; this rejects claims that it is earned by the Messenger's abundant worship or determined by the recipients' original constitution, since a favor is not deserved.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك رد على من قال : إنها تستحق لكثرة طاعة الرسول - ورد على من قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All events happen through God: gnostics know, the spirits of the truthful find intimacy, monotheists' understanding stands before divine majesty, worshippers admit they cannot deserve worship, and all confess they cannot know God's grandeur.
rows.anchor: الحادثات بالله حصلت ، فقلوب العارفين بالله عرفت ما عرفت وأرواح الصديقين بالله ألفت من ألفت وفهوم الموحدين بساحات جلاله وقفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muzzammil means the one wrapped or covered in his clothes.
rows.anchor: أي : المتزمل المتلفف في ثيابه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report says that at the verse's revelation the Prophet and ʿĀʾisha shared a woolen cloak while he prayed; she said it was fourteen cubits long.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : نصفه علي وأنا نائمة ، ونصفه على رسول الله وهو يصلي ، وطول المرط أربعة عشر ذراعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night vigil was initially obligatory, with the Prophet allowed to pray approximately one-third to one-half of the night or somewhat more; after the five prayers became obligatory it was abrogated for the community but remained obligatory for him.
rows.anchor: قم نصف الليل ، وأنقص من النصف

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: A Sufi address calls Muhammad to rise at night under the burdens of prophethood.
rows.anchor: ويقال : يا أيها المتزمل بأعباء النبوة

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another address tells the one concealing what God specially granted him to rise, warn, and trust in divine support.
rows.anchor: ويقال : يا أيها الذي يخفي ما خصصناه به قم فأنذر . . فإنا نصرناك

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another address says that while all others rest at night, the one appointed by God should rise for Him.
rows.anchor: ويقالك قم بنا . . يا من جعلنا الليل ليسكن فيه كل الناس . . قم أنت

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: One explanation says God speaks of Himself in commanding the Prophet's night vigil for the community, honoring his rank and capacity.
rows.anchor: ويقال : لما فرض عليه القيام بالليل أخبر عن نفسه لأجل أمته إكراما لشأنه وقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God descends each night to the lowest heaven; Qushayrī leaves uncertain whether the report's interpretation is known, while lovers have abundant comforts and gifts before that question is resolved.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر : ( أنه ينزل كل ليلة إلى السماء الدنيا . . . ) ولا يدرى التأويل للخبر ، أو أن التأويل معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl means letting the inner self dwell on the Qur'an's meaning and reciting slowly with the tongue.
rows.anchor: ارتع بسرك في فهمه ، وتأن بلسانك في قراءته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation identifies the heavy word as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو القرآن

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Another explanation identifies the heavy word as the declaration that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كلمة لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another explanation identifies it as revelation; it is light on the tongue yet heavy on the scales, or weighty and momentous.
rows.anchor: ويقال : الوحي ؛ وسماه ثقيلا أي خفيفا على اللسان ثقيلا في الميزان . ويقال : ثقيل أي : له وزن وخطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when revelation came while the Prophet rode his camel, it lowered its chest and scarcely moved until the revelation lifted.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر ( كان إذا نزل عليه القرآن - وهو على ناقته - وضعت جرانها ، ولا تكاد تتحرك حتى يسرى عنه )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Sūrat al-Anʿām descended all at once, and the Prophet's camel knelt under the Qur'an's weight and majesty.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن عباس : أن سورة الأنعام نزلت مرة واحدة فبركت ناقة رسول الله من ثقل القرآن وهيبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine name gives clarity to those hearing through knowledge but bewilderment to those hearing through gnosis; scholars rest in proofs, while gnostics are overwhelmed by divine power and self-erasure.
rows.anchor: من سمعها بشاهد العلم استبصر ، ومن سمعها بشاهد المعرفة تحير . . . فالعلماء في سكون برهانه ، والعارفون في دهش سلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase lā uqsim means that God does swear by the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي : أقسم بيوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-reproaching soul is one that censures its owner and recognizes its own deficient state.
rows.anchor: وهي النفس التي تلوم صاحبها ، وتعرف نقصان حالها

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another view says every soul will blame itself tomorrow, either for its unbelief or for its shortcomings; on this view the oath is by the Lord of the self-reproaching soul.
rows.anchor: ويقال : غدا . . . كل نفس تلوم نفسها : إما على كفرها ، وإما على تقصيرها - وعلى هذا فالقسم يكون بإضمار ( الرب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though universal blame has little significance in the Resurrection, the point is that all souls will then be in this condition.
rows.anchor: وليس للوم النفس في القيامة خطر - وإن حمل على الكل ولكن الفائدة فيه بيان أن كل النفوس غدا - ستكون على هذه الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to the oath is balā, meaning yes indeed.
rows.anchor: وجواب القسم قوله : { بلى } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether a person thinks God will not resurrect him after death.
rows.anchor: أيظن أنا لن نبعثه بعد موته

words: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qādirīn is accusative as a circumstantial expression: God is able at that time to restore the fingertips.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال ؛ أي بلى ، نسوي بنانه في الوقت قادرين ، ونقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can make the person's fingers and toes one form, like a camel's hoof or a sheep's cloven hoof; if this is possible, resurrection is certainly possible.
rows.anchor: ونقدر أي نجعل أصابع يديه ورجليه شيئا واحدا كخف البعير وظلف الشاة . . فكيف لا نقدر على إعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person intends to persist in sin, postponing repentance by saying he will repent later, but dies without repenting.
rows.anchor: يقدم الزلة ويؤخر التوبة . ويقول : سوف أتوب ، ثم يموت ولا يتوب

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another reading is that a person resolves not to commit many sins later but remains attached to persisting in the current lapse, so his repentance is invalid; true repentance requires resolving not to return.
rows.anchor: ويقال : يعزم على ألا يستكثر من معاصيه في مستأنف وقته ، وبهذا لا تنحل - في الوقت - عقدة الإصرار من قلبه ، وبذلك لا تصح توبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person still savors sin and thinks of returning to it, his remorse is not valid because he has not truly renounced it.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان استحلاء الزلة في قلبه ، ويفكر في الرجوع إلى مثلها - فلا تصح ندامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person asks when the Resurrection will be because he considers it far-fetched.
rows.anchor: على جهة الاستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, bariqa means the sight is bewildered; with fatḥa, bariqa means the person stares fixedly without blinking from the brilliance.
rows.anchor: { برق } بكسر الراء معناها تحير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people are driven to Hell, it has seventy thousand chains, each held by seventy thousand angels, and every angel and messenger cries, 'Myself, myself!'
rows.anchor: وذلك حين يقاد إلى جهنم بسبعين ألف سلسلة ، كل سلسلة بيد سبعين ألف ملك ، لها زفير وشهيق ، فلا يبقى ملك ولا رسول إلا وهو يقول : نفسي نفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One image compares the sun and moon to two injured bulls brought together.
rows.anchor: كأنهما ثوران عقيران

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Another explanation says they are joined so that neither has any light.
rows.anchor: ويقال : يجمع بينهما في ألا نور لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When these events occur, the person asks where escape can be found.
rows.anchor: يقول الإنسان يومئذ أين المفر
